gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Denon's own US store lists the DCD-600NE at $499 but Out of Stock with a 'Notify me' button, that Onkyo's US site no longer resolves a C-7030 page (onkyousa.com redirects to onkyo.com, no CD-player collection), and that a shopper wanting both optical and coaxial outputs under $500 is left choosing between the Yamaha CD-S303 ($499.95 at Turntable Lab) and the NAD C 538 ($499, Turntable Lab), with the Cambridge AXC35 ($449, Cambridge US) carrying coaxial only.
standout_why: insideouthomereviews.com (read 2026-11-08) prices Yamaha CD-S303 $449.95, Denon DCD-600NE $399.50 and NAD C 538 $499 from Amazon as of 2026-11-07 and lists outputs/USB/warranty, but says nothing about maker stock status, does not cover Onkyo C-7030, Cambridge AXC35, Marantz CD60, Yamaha CD-C603 or any sub-$200 options with optical/line out. Crutchfield, Yamaha USA, B&H and Sweetwater pages returned 403 so their content could not be checked; the Yamaha and Onkyo manual PDFs carry specs but no prices. The maker-store availability of the Denon and the disappearance of the Onkyo from the US site are new; Marantz US pricing is new.
decides: Confirms the Yamaha CD-S303 as the default pick for a plain stereo: it is the only sub-$500 component with RCA + optical + coaxial + USB playback, while the cheaper Denon is optical-only, out of stock at Denon US, and the Onkyo C-7030 has no live maker page. The NAD C 538 ties on outputs at the same street price but has no USB. If the shopper's amp has only an optical input or they want a headphone jack, the $139.99 Fosi Audio Merak or $164.99 FiiO DM13 become the budget alternative; the Marantz CD60 at $1,100 is the step up with 118 dB S/N and a headphone jack.
